query: For an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy in its uniform, fine lamellar state, whose strength and plasticity remain below industrial application requirements, what single intervention could improve performance for fasteners exposed to extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosive conditions? State the proposed intervention, mechanism, predicted outcome relative to the starting alloy, applicable operating and test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit falsification criteria.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a minor amount of zirconium to the as-cast Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy will refine the fine lamellar microstructure and promote the formation of zirconium-rich precipitates, leading to crack arrest and improved mechanical integrity under extreme service conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy in a uniform, fine lamellar structure with suboptimal strength and plasticity.
generation.intervention: Introduce a controlled addition of zirconium (by weight percent, e.g., around 1–2 wt%) into the melt during alloy production.
generation.conditions: Intended for fasteners that face extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosive environments.
generation.structural_mediator: Refinement of the lamellar microstructure along with the formation of stable zirconium-rich phases (e.g., Zr-based intermetallics or precipitates) that act as barriers to grain boundary sliding and crack propagation.
generation.mechanism: Zirconium addition promotes heterogeneous nucleation during solidification, leading to a decrease in lamellar spacing and improved phase stability; this refined microstructure enhances dislocation pinning, reduces creep deformation, and improves resistance to corrosion and cyclic thermal stresses.
generation.predicted_outcome: The zirconium-alloyed variant is expected to display higher yield strength and tensile ductility, improved creep resistance at room temperature, and better corrosion resistance compared to the original alloy.
generation.baseline: The original Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni2.1 alloy exhibits inadequate performance for fastener applications under extreme temperature and load conditions, as indicated by its lower strength and limited plasticity.
generation.boundary: The improvements are predicted to be effective within the operational temperature extremes, mechanical loading regimes, and corrosive conditions typical of fastener applications; however, the exact zirconium content and processing conditions may require optimization to avoid over-stabilization that could lead to embrittlement.
generation.uncertainty: The precise quantitative improvements in mechanical and corrosion properties, as well as the optimum zirconium concentration for balancing strength and ductility, remain uncertain and dependent on alloy processing and service conditions.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of alloy samples: one following the original Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni2.1 composition and one with the zirconium addition (1–2 wt%). Process both sets under identical conditions to achieve similar lamellar structures. Subject samples from each set to a battery of tests including tensile strength, ductility, room-temperature creep, thermal cycling (to simulate extreme temperature fluctuations), and corrosion resistance tests in relevant environments.
measurements: Tensile stress-strain curves to determine yield strength and ductility.
Creep rate measurements under constant load at room temperature.
Thermal cycling tests to evaluate microstructural stability and fatigue resistance.
Electrochemical corrosion tests to assess resistance in corrosive media.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the zirconium-alloyed samples do not demonstrate statistically significant improvement in mechanical (yield strength, ductility, creep resistance) and corrosion properties under the test conditions compared to the baseline alloy, the hypothesis of improved performance due to zirconium addition would be falsified.
